correctness.rationale: For complex H, N in S_p with N²=0 (p>=1), polar source/range supports are orthogonal. Direct products of X=(|N*|^{1/2}-|N|^{1/2})/2 and Y=U|N|^{1/2} give XY=N/2, YX=-N/2, S_{2p} norm-product 2^{1/(2p)-1}||N||_p. For unrestricted factors the dual W=|N|^{p-1}U* lies in a square-zero corner. The corner commutator bound interpolates the HS endpoint sqrt(2)||W||∞||X||₂, proved by orthogonal block energy, with trace endpoint 2||W||₁||X||∞, yielding 2^{1-1/(2p)}||W||_{p'}||X||_{2p} in S_{2p/(2p-1)}. Polar powers W(z),X(z),Z(z) on the strip yield the exact exponent; finite-rank density and trace duality cover infinite rank and p=1. Trace cyclicity gives the matching lower bound over ALL factors. Independently verified explicit multi-singular examples p=1,1.3,2,4,10 and 300 random complex-matrix HS corner tests; these do not prove the infinite-dimensional interpolation.
residual_risks: Bounded checks corroborate; unrestricted claim depends on analytical proof.

originality.rationale: Liu–Yang 2026 Thm 1.1 establishes general single commutator existence p>2 with upper bound 16 zeta(p−1)^{1/p}, not the sharp infimum. Dykema–Krishnaswamy-Usha handle ideal membership for nilpotent commutators; Marcoux–Radjavi–Zhang constrain square-zero FACTORS, a different problem. Resultary normal finite-rank target result estimates norm costs up to constants, not nonnormal index-two nilpotents. Rank-one p=1 is classical Hilbert–Schmidt comparison; the all-rank all-p exact cost appears additional, subject to alternate formulations of sharp corner interpolation.
